title.narrative: Independent Third Party Monitoring (TPM) of selected FCDO-funded emergency programmes to support and maximise UK Aid delivery in DRC – Year II.

description.narrative: To provide independent oversight by combining regular light-touch verification with in-depth thematic analysis to provide FCDO and partners with data and action points to contribute to increased aid effectiveness, accountability and evidence-based response planning. With the overall objective of both strengthening FCDO-funded aid interventions’ and partners’ effectiveness and efficiency, IMPACT Initiatives proposes to provide third party monitoring.

participating-org.ref: UK - Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

recipient-country.narrative: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) faces one of the world’s most complex and long-standing humanitarian crises. In 2020, the country saw COVID-19 exacerbating existing vulnerabilities alongside a resurgence in armed conflict and violence, and 27 million people are currently in dire need of protection and humanitarian assistance (Humanitarian Needs Overview, 2022) - an increase of more than 5 million, especially due to the IPC food insecurity analysis. A combination of protracted conflict in parts of the country and additional shocks, including natural disasters and epidemics, has resulted in high sustained levels of humanitarian needs and large-scale population movement, with 5.7 million people affected by population movements in DRC, according to the 2022 HNO. In light of this fluid context, in particular in provinces in eastern DRC, where new shocks regularly lead to shifting needs and population movement, emergency programming including through rapid response mechanisms, such as those funded by FCDO. An FCDO-funded ODI publication identified an increasing trend of cash and voucher programming in the DRC humanitarian response. There is a lack of independent verification of large-scale humanitarian interventions to ensure quality, appropriate design, and impact on affected communities. Moreover, humanitarian assistance delivered to vulnerable populations in DRC, including through rapid response mechanisms and cash modalities, suffered from various aid integrity risks, as found in the Humanitarian Country Team and Joint Anti‐Fraud Taskforce-commissioned Operational Review, published in July 2020. Aid integrity has been found to be a significant issue within the DRC humanitarian response, with exposure of fraud and sexual exploitation cases. Despite efforts made by humanitarian actors, the review outlines a number of gaps and measures that would decrease the occurrence of fraudulent systems. Third Party Monitoring (TPM) is referenced in the review as one of the potential avenues mitigating the challenges of monitoring and evaluating programme implementation in high risk contexts. For the year to March 2022, IMPACT Initiatives has been delivering a Third Party Monitoring (TPM) pilot of selected FCDO-funded humanitarian interventions of the World Food Programme (WFP) and two partners under the SAFER (Strategic Assistance for Humanitarian Response in DRC) consortium partners (Mercy Corps and Solidarités International). In line with the overall sector focus as well as the identification of risks, this TPM has focused on cash and transfer interventions, especially those taking place in harder-to-reach locations. This current TPM is set to include six visits with resulting reports including practical recommendations, as well as an overall thematic piece on Accountability to Affected Populations.
